description: Published HDC/VSA benchmark results curated from arXiv abstracts for Program 3 research ingestion.

entries.name: Primitive-Driven Acceleration of Hyperdimensional Computing for Real-Time Image Classification
entries.key_finding: FPGA implementation reports 0.09 ms inference latency with up to 1300x speedup over CPU and 60x over GPU baselines while improving image-encoder accuracy.

entries.name: SpecHD: Hyperdimensional Computing Framework for FPGA-based Mass Spectrometry Clustering
entries.key_finding: Processes a 25 million-spectrum (131 GB) human proteome dataset in 5 minutes with energy efficiency over 31x and speedup ranging 6x to 54x versus state of the art.

entries.name: Massively Parallel Open Modification Spectral Library Searching with Hyperdimensional Computing
entries.dimensions_tested: high-dimensional binary vectors (exact D not reported in abstract)
entries.accuracy_pct: comparable search quality (no explicit percentage in abstract)
entries.key_finding: HyperOMS on GPU is reported up to 17x faster and 6.4x more energy efficient than the state-of-the-art GPU OMS baseline while maintaining comparable search quality.

entries.name: MIMHD: Accurate and Efficient Hyperdimensional Inference Using Multi-Bit In-Memory Computing
entries.comparison_baseline: binary HDC implementations and GPU baselines
entries.key_finding: At D=4000 on six datasets, 3-bit MIMHD reports 92.6% average accuracy with 84.1x energy improvement and 38.4x speedup over GPU; 2-bit mode reports 88.9% with similar efficiency gains.

entries.name: FeReX: A Reconfigurable Design of Multi-bit Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory for Nearest Neighbor Search
entries.key_finding: For KNN and HDC benchmarks, FeReX reports up to 250x speedup and 10^4 energy savings compared with GPU.

entries.name: SEE-MCAM: Scalable Multi-bit FeFET Content Addressable Memories for Energy Efficient Associative Search
entries.comparison_baseline: CMOS CAM, ReRAM/FeFET MCAM, GPU HDC implementation
entries.key_finding: Reports 3-bit-per-cell CAM, 9.8x energy-efficiency gain and 1.6x lower search latency vs CMOS CAM, plus up to three orders-of-magnitude speed/energy improvement over GPU for quantized HDC acceleration.

entries.name: HyperSense: Hyperdimensional Intelligent Sensing for Energy-Efficient Sparse Data Processing
entries.accuracy_pct: best AUC/ROC among lightweight models (exact percentage not reported in abstract)
entries.comparison_baseline: YOLOv4 on NVIDIA Jetson Orin and conventional sensing pipeline
entries.key_finding: HyperSense reports 5.6x speedup versus YOLOv4 on Jetson Orin and up to 92.1% energy savings compared with conventional systems.

entries.name: Hyperdimensional Computing for ADHD Classification using EEG Signals
entries.comparison_baseline: traditional deep neural network benchmark models
entries.key_finding: The proposed HDC model reports 88.9% ADHD classification accuracy and indicates comparable performance using only 7 of 79 patients for training relative to full-data baselines.

entries.name: Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks Using Hyperdimensional Computing: A Case Study on the NSL-KDD Dataset
entries.key_finding: On NSL-KDD, the HDC intrusion detection framework reports 99.54% accuracy and outperforms conventional IDS approaches across attack classes including DoS, probe, R2L, and U2R.

entries.name: VS-Graph: Scalable and Efficient Graph Classification Using Hyperdimensional Computing
entries.accuracy_pct: 4-5 percentage-point gain over prior HDC baseline
entries.comparison_baseline: prior HDC baseline and multiple GNN baselines
entries.hardware: edge and neuromorphic deployment context (no specific platform in abstract)
entries.key_finding: VS-Graph reports 4-5% accuracy improvement over prior HDC graph methods and up to 450x training acceleration while remaining robust at D=128.
